## formal
Let $k$ be $\Q$ or an ordered field and $\Cl_{k}(\ell,\ell)$ the algebra of $\ell$ modes of Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}: generators $e_{j}$, $f_{j}$ with $Q(e_{j}) = 1$, $Q(f_{j}) = -1$, null pairs $v_{j} = \tfrac12(e_{j} + f_{j})$, $w_{j} = \tfrac12(e_{j} - f_{j})$, with $v_{i}w_{j} + w_{j}v_{i} = \delta_{ij}$; let $V$ be the span of the generators, $W$ the span of the $v_{j}$ and $W'$ the span of the $w_{j}$ (isotropic, $V = W \oplus W'$). A \emph{split} is a decomposition $V = V_{+} \oplus V_{-}$ into orthogonal subspaces on which $Q$ is positive and negative definite; its \emph{adjoint} is the anti-automorphism $\dagger_{s}$ of the algebra that is $+1$ on $V_{+}$ and $-1$ on $V_{-}$. The stored split, $V_{+}$ spanned by the $e_{j}$ and $V_{-}$ by the $f_{j}$, has the blade inverse $\dagger$ as adjoint. A split is \emph{adapted} (to the null pairs) if its adjoint maps $W$ onto $W'$. Premise (P), positivity of values (Premise \claimref{synthesis.premise-positivity-of-values}; assumed, not derived), is stated relative to a split: a state for the split $s$ is a $k$-linear $\omega$ with $\omega(1) = 1$, $\omega(xx^{\dagger_{s}}) \ge 0$ and $\omega(x^{\dagger_{s}}) = \omega(x)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The null pairs fix the split up to a positive form; proved.)} The adapted splits correspond one to one to the positive definite symmetric bilinear forms $g$ on $W$, by $g(v,v') = vv'^{\dagger_{s}} + v'^{\dagger_{s}}v$; the stored split has $g(v_{i},v_{j}) = \delta_{ij}$. For $A \in \mathrm{GL}_{\ell}(k)$ the vectors $v'_{j} = \sum_{i}A_{ij}v_{i}$, $w'_{j} = \sum_{i}(A^{-1})_{ji}w_{i}$ are null pairs spanning the same $W$, $W'$, and $e'_{j} = v'_{j} + w'_{j}$, $f'_{j} = v'_{j} - w'_{j}$ is an orthonormal frame of an adapted split. For $\ell = 1$ the adapted splits are the frames $e' = tv_{1} + t^{-1}w_{1}$, $f' = tv_{1} - t^{-1}w_{1}$, $t \ne 0$, with the same two null lines and the same parity $f'e' = f_{1}e_{1}$; $t = 4$ is the boosted frame $\tfrac{17}{8}e_{1} + \tfrac{15}{8}f_{1}$, $\tfrac{15}{8}e_{1} + \tfrac{17}{8}f_{1}$ of clause (vi) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate}. So the null pairs that define the modes do not determine the adjoint of (P); what is missing is a positive definite form on $W$, $\ell(\ell+1)/2$ numbers.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(What the null pairs do fix; proved.)} The number element $N = \sum_{j}w_{j}v_{j}$ is the same for every pair of dual bases of $W$ and $W'$, and $N^{\dagger_{s}} = N$ for every adapted split. Hence the sector projectors $Q_{n} = \prod_{m \ne n}(N - m)/(n - m)$, $0 \le n \le \ell$ (idempotent, with sum $1$ and $\langle Q_{n}\rangle_{0} = \binom{\ell}{n}2^{-\ell}$), the vacuum projector $Q_{0}$ and the total parity are self-adjoint for every adapted split.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The functionals real for every adapted split; proved, with the case $\ell = 2$ by a complete finite computation.)} A $k$-linear functional $\omega$ satisfies $\omega(x^{\dagger_{s}}) = \omega(x)$ for all $x$ and all adapted splits $s$ if and only if $\omega(x) = \langle h(N)x\rangle_{0}$ for a polynomial $h$ of degree at most $\ell$: a space of dimension $\ell + 1$. Such a functional is a state for one adapted split if and only if it is a state for all of them, if and only if $\omega = \sum_{n}q_{n}\,\langle Q_{n}x\rangle_{0}/\langle Q_{n}\rangle_{0}$ with $q_{n} \ge 0$ and $\sum_{n}q_{n} = 1$. These are the states of (P) that do not depend on the choice of adapted split; they include the vacuum state, the state of $Q_{\ell}$ and the products $\prod_{j}\tfrac12(1 + rp_{j})$ with one common $r$, $|r| \le 1$, $p_{j} = f_{j}e_{j}$. If only the splits adapted to each mode separately are admitted ($g$ diagonal in the $v_{j}$), the functionals real for all of them are the $\langle h(w_{1}v_{1}, \dots, w_{\ell}v_{\ell})x\rangle_{0}$, a space of dimension $2^{\ell}$, which contains every product $\prod_{j}\tfrac12(1 + r_{j}p_{j})$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(States that need the split; proved.)} Every other state of the stored split fails to be a state for some adapted split. In particular the pair state $\rho_{12}$ of clause (v) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-algebra-and-its-klein-twist-to-the-tensor-product} with $cs \ne 0$ is not real for the split with $v'_{1} = 2v_{1}$ (at $c = \tfrac35$, $s = \tfrac45$ its values on $w_{1}w_{2}$ and on the adjoint of $w_{1}w_{2}$ for that split are $\tfrac{12}{25}$ and $\tfrac{48}{25}$). For $\ell = 2$ and the directions $a_{i} = x_{i}e_{1} + z_{i}p_{1}$, $b_{j} = x'_{j}e_{2}p_{1} + z'_{j}p_{2}$ of clause (vii) of the CHSH theorem, a state of the family (iii) gives the CHSH element the value $Z\,\omega(p_{1}p_{2})$, $Z = z_{1}(z'_{1} + z'_{2}) + z_{2}(z'_{1} - z'_{2})$, of absolute value at most $2$: in that setting a value above $2$ requires a state that depends on the split.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Scope.} A state for one split assigns numbers in $[0,1]$ to the projectors of that split only; for an idempotent that is self-adjoint for another adapted split its value can lie outside $[0,1]$, as in the stored example with the value $\tfrac{17}{4}$. The statements are about the algebras $\Cl_{k}(\ell,\ell)$ and the splits adapted to their null pairs. Splits that are not adapted exist for $\ell \ge 2$ and are not treated. Nothing here says which split, if any, the series' other premises select.

## technical
Premise (P), positivity of values, is stated relative to a split of the generators into those of square $+1$ and those of square $-1$, because the adjoint is defined by the split; (P) is assumed, not derived. For the mode algebras $\Cl_{k}(\ell,\ell)$ this result says how much of the split the modes themselves fix. The modes are given by null pairs $v_{j}$, $w_{j}$, that is, by two complementary isotropic subspaces $W$ and $W'$. The splits whose adjoint exchanges $W$ and $W'$ correspond exactly to the positive definite forms on $W$: for one mode a single positive number, the scale $t$ in $e' = tv + w/t$, and the stored boosted frame with the value $17/4$ of the CHSH combination is $t = 4$. So the null pairs do not determine the adjoint. They do determine the number element $N$, its sector projectors, the vacuum projector and the total parity, which are self-adjoint for every adapted split.

Under (P) for a given split, the states that are states for every adapted split are exactly the mixtures of the normalised sector projectors of $N$: a family with $\ell$ free weights, containing the vacuum and the product states with one common occupation for all modes. If the scale of each mode is free but the modes are kept apart, the common states are the number-diagonal ones, which include all thermal products. Every state with coherence between sectors, such as the stored pair states, is tied to one split; and with one mode per party the split-independent states give the CHSH combination at most $2$. The correspondence, the invariance of $N$ and the classification are proved; the classification uses scalings of single modes and a complete finite computation for two modes.

## lay
The series' assumption (P) about averages uses a mirror operation on the algebra, and that operation depends on dividing the basic directions into two kinds. Given that assumption and the series' description of its modes by pairs of light-like directions, this result asks how much of the division those pairs fix. The answer is: not all of it. For one mode a single positive number, a scale, is left free; for several modes a whole table of such numbers. A known example in the series where the limit on correlations seems to be broken is just a change of this scale.

Assuming (P), the result then finds which states make sense whatever the scale is: only those that are a mixture of "this many modes are occupied" with nothing more specific, such as the empty state or a thermal state with the same occupation for every mode. States in which two modes are entangled depend on the scale, and under the same assumption the states that do not depend on it never exceed the classical limit 2 in the simplest two-party arrangement. So some further datum of the theory has to supply the scale; the result does not say which.

## one-liner
In $\Cl_{k}(\ell,\ell)$ the null pairs fix the split behind the adjoint of (P) only up to a positive definite form on their isotropic span (for one mode a scale $t$; $t = 4$ is the stored boosted frame); given (P), the states common to all adapted splits are exactly the mixtures of the sector projectors of the number element, and with one mode per party they give the CHSH element at most $2$.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Preliminaries.} Write $\tau = \langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$ and $u \cdot u' = \tfrac12(uu' + u'u)$ for vectors. By Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}, $W$ and $W'$ are isotropic and $2v_{i} \cdot w_{j} = \delta_{ij}$, so the form pairs $W$ with $W'$ perfectly. An orthogonal linear map $M$ of $V$ extends uniquely to an automorphism and (composed with the reverse) to an anti-automorphism of the algebra; the adjoint of a split is the anti-automorphism extending the reflection $M_{s}$ that is $+1$ on $V_{+}$ and $-1$ on $V_{-}$, and for the stored split it is the blade inverse of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate} (it fixes $e_{j}$ and negates $f_{j}$). The composition of two adjoints is the automorphism extending the product of the two reflections.

\emph{(i).} Let $s$ be adapted and $M = M_{s}$. For $v, v' \in W$, $g(v,v') = 2v \cdot Mv'$; it is symmetric because $M$ is an orthogonal involution ($v \cdot Mv' = Mv \cdot M^{2}v' = Mv \cdot v'$). For $v \ne 0$ the vector $v + Mv$ is fixed by $M$, so it lies in $V_{+}$, and it is nonzero because $W \cap W' = 0$; hence $0 < Q(v + Mv) = 2v \cdot Mv = g(v,v)$, using $Q(v) = Q(Mv) = 0$. Conversely let $g$ be positive definite and symmetric on $W$, and let $\theta : W \to W'$ be the linear map with $2v \cdot \theta v' = g(v,v')$ (it exists and is injective because the pairing is perfect and $g$ nondegenerate). Put $V_{\pm} = \{v \pm \theta v\}$. Then $Q(v \pm \theta v) = \pm g(v,v)$, $(v + \theta v) \cdot (v' - \theta v') = \tfrac12(-g(v,v') + g(v',v)) = 0$, and $V_{+} \cap V_{-} = 0$, so by dimension $V = V_{+} \oplus V_{-}$ is a split; its reflection sends $v$ to $\theta v$, so it is adapted and its form is $g$. The two constructions are inverse to each other. For $A \in \mathrm{GL}_{\ell}(k)$: $2v'_{i} \cdot w'_{j} = \sum_{a}A_{ai}(A^{-1})_{ja} = \delta_{ij}$, so the $e'_{j}$, $f'_{j}$ are orthonormal with squares $1$, $-1$, the reflection of this frame exchanges $v'_{j}$ and $w'_{j}$, and the split is adapted. For $\ell = 1$ and $A = (t)$: $e' = tv_{1} + t^{-1}w_{1} = \tfrac12(t + t^{-1})e_{1} + \tfrac12(t - t^{-1})f_{1}$, which at $t = 4$ is $\tfrac{17}{8}e_{1} + \tfrac{15}{8}f_{1}$, and $f'e' = (tv_{1} - t^{-1}w_{1})(tv_{1} + t^{-1}w_{1}) = v_{1}w_{1} - w_{1}v_{1} = f_{1}e_{1}$. The space of symmetric forms on $W$ has dimension $\ell(\ell+1)/2$.

\emph{(ii).} If $v'_{j} = \sum_{i}A_{ij}v_{i}$ is another basis of $W$ and $w'_{j}$ the dual basis of $W'$, then $w'_{j} = \sum_{i}(A^{-1})_{ji}w_{i}$ and $\sum_{j}w'_{j}v'_{j} = \sum_{i,a}\bigl(\sum_{j}(A^{-1})_{ji}A_{aj}\bigr)w_{i}v_{a} = \sum_{i}w_{i}v_{i}$. For an adapted split with form $g$ choose a basis $v'_{j}$ of $W$ and put $w'_{j} = v_{j}'^{\dagger_{s}} \in W'$; if $g$ has an orthonormal basis this gives dual bases and $N^{\dagger_{s}} = \sum_{j}(w'_{j}v'_{j})^{\dagger_{s}} = \sum_{j}w'_{j}v'_{j} = N$. In general let $G_{ij} = g(v'_{i},v'_{j})$; the dual basis of $W'$ is $\sum_{i}(G^{-1})_{ji}w'_{i}$, so $N = \sum_{i,j}(G^{-1})_{ji}w'_{i}v'_{j}$ and $N^{\dagger_{s}} = \sum_{i,j}(G^{-1})_{ji}w'_{j}v'_{i} = N$ because $G$ is symmetric. The elements $n_{j} = w_{j}v_{j}$ are commuting idempotents ($w_{j}v_{j}w_{j}v_{j} = w_{j}(1 - w_{j}v_{j})v_{j} = w_{j}v_{j}$), so $N$ satisfies $\prod_{m=0}^{\ell}(N - m) = 0$, the $Q_{n}$ are the idempotents of its spectral decomposition, polynomials in $N$, hence self-adjoint for every adapted split; $Q_{n}$ is the sum of the $\binom{\ell}{n}$ products $\prod_{j \in I}n_{j}\prod_{j \notin I}(1 - n_{j})$, $|I| = n$, each of scalar part $2^{-\ell}$ since $n_{j} = \tfrac12(1 - p_{j})$; and the total parity is $\prod_{j}(1 - 2n_{j}) = \sum_{n}(-1)^{n}Q_{n}$.

\emph{(iii).} The condition is linear in $\omega$. Sufficiency: $h(N)$ is self-adjoint for every adapted split by (ii), and $\tau(x^{\dagger_{s}}) = \tau(x)$ for every split (an anti-automorphism extending an orthogonal map preserves the scalar part), so $\tau(h(N)x^{\dagger_{s}}) = \tau((xh(N))^{\dagger_{s}}) = \tau(h(N)x)$. The functionals $\tau(N^{j}\,\cdot)$, $0 \le j \le \ell$, are independent because $1, N, \dots, N^{\ell}$ are and $\tau(y^{\dagger}y) > 0$ for $y \ne 0$. Necessity. Step 1: let $\omega$ be real for the stored split and for the split with $A = \operatorname{diag}(t_{1}, \dots, t_{\ell})$. Then $\omega$ is invariant under the composition of the two adjoints, the automorphism with $v_{j} \mapsto t_{j}^{2}v_{j}$, $w_{j} \mapsto t_{j}^{-2}w_{j}$. The ordered monomials $w_{I}v_{J}$ ($I$, $J$ subsets of the modes) are a basis, and this automorphism multiplies $w_{I}v_{J}$ by $\prod_{j \in J}t_{j}^{2}\prod_{i \in I}t_{i}^{-2}$; taking $t_{j} = 2$ for one $j$ in the symmetric difference of $I$ and $J$ and $t = 1$ elsewhere gives $\omega(w_{I}v_{J}) = 0$ unless $I = J$. So $\omega$ is determined by the numbers $c_{I} = \omega(\prod_{j \in I}n_{j})$; this already proves the statement about splits adapted to each mode separately (dimension $2^{\ell}$; sufficiency there as above, the $n_{j}$ being self-adjoint for such splits). Step 2, $\ell = 2$: the script computes the space of functionals real for the four splits $A = 1$, $\operatorname{diag}(2,1)$, $\operatorname{diag}(1,3)$ and the shear $v'_{2} = v_{1} + v_{2}$; it has dimension $3$ and equals the span of $\tau(N^{j}\,\cdot)$, $j = 0, 1, 2$. The conditions have rational coefficients, so the dimension is the same over every $k$. In particular $c_{\{1\}} = c_{\{2\}}$. Step 3, general $\ell$: fix two modes $i \ne j$ and a set $I$ of other modes, and put $\omega_{I}(y) = \omega(\prod_{m \in I}n_{m}\,y)$ for $y$ in the subalgebra of the modes $i$, $j$. An adapted split of that two-mode algebra, extended by the stored split on the other modes, is an adapted split of the whole, its adjoint fixes $\prod_{m \in I}n_{m}$, which commutes with $y$; so $\omega_{I}$ is real for every adapted split of the two modes, and by Step 2 $\omega_{I}(n_{i}) = \omega_{I}(n_{j})$, that is $c_{I \cup \{i\}} = c_{I \cup \{j\}}$. Hence $c_{I}$ depends only on $|I|$, the space has dimension at most $\ell + 1$, and with sufficiency it is the span of the $\tau(N^{j}\,\cdot)$; the script confirms dimension $4$ for $\ell = 3$. States, in the sense of Premise \claimref{synthesis.premise-positivity-of-values} read for the split $s$: write $h(N) = \sum_{n}h(n)Q_{n}$. If $\omega$ is a state for one adapted split then $\omega(Q_{n}) = h(n)\tau(Q_{n}) \ge 0$, as $Q_{n} = Q_{n}Q_{n}^{\dagger_{s}}$, and $\sum_{n}h(n)\tau(Q_{n}) = 1$; conversely for every adapted split each $x \mapsto \tau(Q_{n}x)/\tau(Q_{n})$ is a state (the functional of an element $Q_{n}Q_{n}^{\dagger_{s}}$; clause (iii) of the CHSH theorem, whose proof applies to the blade inverse of any orthonormal frame, and for a split without orthonormal frame over $k$ by extending $k$), so the convex combinations are. The vacuum state is $q_{0} = 1$; $\prod_{j}\tfrac12(1 + rp_{j}) = \prod_{j}\bigl(\tfrac{1+r}{2}(1 - n_{j}) + \tfrac{1-r}{2}n_{j}\bigr)$ is a function of the $n_{j}$ symmetric in them with coefficient depending only on the number of occupied modes, hence a function of $N$; with distinct $r_{j}$ it is a function of the $n_{j}$.

\emph{(iv).} A state of the stored split that is a state for every adapted split is real for all of them, hence of the form (iii). For the pair state of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-algebra-and-its-klein-twist-to-the-tensor-product}, clause (v), $\rho_{12}$ contains $cs(w_{1}w_{2} + v_{2}v_{1})$, so its functional $x \mapsto 4\tau(\rho_{12}x)$ is nonzero on the monomial $w_{1}w_{2}$ paired against $v_{2}v_{1}$, a monomial with $I \ne J$, and Step 1 excludes it; the two values are the script's. For the CHSH element: as in the cited clause (vii), $a_{i}b_{j} = x_{i}x'_{j}\,e_{2}f_{1} + x_{i}z'_{j}\,e_{1}p_{2} + z_{i}x'_{j}\,p_{1}e_{2}p_{1} + z_{i}z'_{j}\,p_{1}p_{2}$, using $e_{1}e_{2}p_{1} = e_{2}f_{1}$. The second and third terms are odd, and $e_{2}f_{1} = (v_{2} + w_{2})(v_{1} - w_{1})$ is a combination of monomials $w_{I}v_{J}$ with $I \ne J$ (after ordering, $v_{2}v_{1}$, $w_{1}v_{2}$, $w_{2}v_{1}$, $w_{2}w_{1}$); a functional of the family (iii) vanishes on all of these by Step 1. So $\omega(C) = Z\omega(p_{1}p_{2})$. $|\omega(p_{1}p_{2})| = |q_{0} - q_{1} + q_{2}| \le 1$, and $|Z| \le |z'_{1} + z'_{2}| + |z'_{1} - z'_{2}| \le 2$ since $|z_{i}| \le 1$ and $|z'_{j}| \le 1$.

check_py:
"""synthesis.splits-adapted-to-the-null-pairs-and-the-states-common-to-all-of-them: exact checks.

Cl_Q(l,l): e_k (square +1, index 2k), f_k (square -1, index 2k+1), null pairs v_k = (e_k + f_k)/2,
w_k = (e_k - f_k)/2. For A in GL_l(Q) the adapted split has null pairs v'_j = sum_i A_ij v_i,
w'_j = sum_i (A^-1)_ji w_i and generators e'_j = v'_j + w'_j, f'_j = v'_j - w'_j; its adjoint is the
anti-automorphism that fixes the e'_j and negates the f'_j.

(i)   the adapted frames are orthonormal of squares +1, -1; l = 1, t = 4 is the stored boosted frame.
(ii)  the number element N, the total parity, the vacuum projector and the sector projectors are
      self-adjoint for every adapted split used.
(iii) the functionals real for all the splits used: dimension 2 (l = 1), 3 (l = 2), 4 (l = 3), equal to
      l + 1, spanned by the functionals of 1, N, ..., N^l; for diagonal A only: dimension 2^l (l = 2: 4).
(iv)  a stored pair state is not real for a second adapted split, and the common states give the CHSH
      element of the one-mode twisted directions the value Z * (value of the total parity) only.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

ONE = GA.sc(F(1))
HALF = F(1, 2)


def clean(x):
    return {b: c for b, c in x.items() if c != 0}


def prod(sq, *xs):
    r = ONE
    for x in xs:
        r = GA.mul(r, x, sq)
    return clean(r)


def lin(*terms):
    r = {}
    for c, x in terms:
        r = GA.add(r, GA.scal(F(c), x))
    return clean(r)


def tau(x):
    return x.get((), F(0))


def blade(b):
    return {tuple(b): F(1)}


def modes(m):
    sq = tuple(s for _ in range(m) for s in (1, -1))
    e = [GA.gen(2 * k) for k in range(m)]
    f = [GA.gen(2 * k + 1) for k in range(m)]
    v = [lin((HALF, e[k]), (HALF, f[k])) for k in range(m)]
    w = [lin((HALF, e[k]), (-HALF, f[k])) for k in range(m)]
    return sq, e, f, v, w


def eye(n):
    return [[F(int(i == j)) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]


def shear(n, i, j):
    A, B = eye(n), eye(n)
    A[i][j], B[i][j] = F(1), F(-1)
    return A, B


def scale(n, i, t):
    A, B = eye(n), eye(n)
    A[i][i], B[i][i] = F(t), F(1) / F(t)
    return A, B


def frame(m, A, Ainv):
    sq, e, f, v, w = modes(m)
    vn = [lin(*[(A[i][j], v[i]) for i in range(m)]) for j in range(m)]
    wn = [lin(*[(Ainv[j][i], w[i]) for i in range(m)]) for j in range(m)]
    en = [clean(GA.add(vn[j], wn[j])) for j in range(m)]
    fn = [clean(GA.sub(vn[j], wn[j])) for j in range(m)]
    return sq, en, fn, vn, wn


def frame_is_orthonormal(m, A, Ainv):
    sq, en, fn, vn, wn = frame(m, A, Ainv)
    gens = en + fn
    ok = all(prod(sq, x, x) == ONE for x in en) and all(prod(sq, x, x) == GA.neg(ONE) for x in fn)
    return ok and all(GA.anticommutes(gens[i], gens[j], sq) for i in range(2 * m) for j in range(i))


def reflection(m, A, Ainv):
    """Images of the stored generators under the reflection fixing the e'_j and negating the f'_j."""
    sq, en, fn, vn, wn = frame(m, A, Ainv)
    out = []
    for i in range(2 * m):
        g = GA.gen(i)
        r = {}
        for x in en + fn:
            r = GA.add(r, GA.scal(tau(prod(sq, g, x)), x))
        out.append(clean(r))
    return sq, out


def adjoint(sq, images, x):
    r = {}
    for b, c in x.items():
        y = ONE
        for i in reversed(b):
            y = GA.mul(y, images[i], sq)
        r = GA.add(r, GA.scal(c, y))
    return clean(r)


def common_real(m, mats):
    """Kernel of the conditions omega(x - x^dagger_A) = 0 over all blades x and all splits A in mats."""
    sq = modes(m)[0]
    blades = GA.all_blades(2 * m)
    rows = []
    for A, Ainv in mats:
        _, images = reflection(m, A, Ainv)
        for b in blades:
            d = clean(GA.sub(blade(b), adjoint(sq, images, blade(b))))
            if d:
                rows.append([d.get(bb, F(0)) for bb in blades])
    return GA.field_kernel(rows), blades


def number(m):
    sq, e, f, v, w = modes(m)
    n = {}
    for k in range(m):
        n = GA.add(n, prod(sq, w[k], v[k]))
    return sq, clean(n)


def power_functionals(m):
    """Values on the blades of x -> tau(N^j x), j = 0..m."""
    sq, n = number(m)
    blades = GA.all_blades(2 * m)
    out, y = [], ONE
    for _ in range(m + 1):
        out.append([tau(prod(sq, y, blade(b))) for b in blades])
        y = prod(sq, y, n)
    return out


M1 = [(eye(1), eye(1)), scale(1, 0, 4)]
M2 = [(eye(2), eye(2)), scale(2, 0, 2), scale(2, 1, 3), shear(2, 0, 1)]
M2_DIAGONAL = [(eye(2), eye(2)), scale(2, 0, 2), scale(2, 1, 3)]
M3 = [(eye(3), eye(3)), scale(3, 0, 2), scale(3, 1, 3), scale(3, 2, 5), shear(3, 0, 1), shear(3, 1, 2)]


def check_adapted_frames_and_the_stored_boosted_frame():
    premise("tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors")
    premise("synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate")
    assert all(frame_is_orthonormal(1, *m) for m in M1) and all(frame_is_orthonormal(2, *m) for m in M2)
    assert all(frame_is_orthonormal(3, *m) for m in M3)
    sq, en, fn, vn, wn = frame(1, *scale(1, 0, 4))
    e, f = GA.gen(0), GA.gen(1)
    assert en[0] == lin((F(17, 8), e), (F(15, 8), f)) and fn[0] == lin((F(15, 8), e), (F(17, 8), f))
    assert prod(sq, fn[0], en[0]) == prod(sq, f, e)
    # the adjoint of the identity split is the blade inverse; of the boosted split it is not
    _, im0 = reflection(1, eye(1), eye(1))
    _, im4 = reflection(1, *scale(1, 0, 4))
    assert adjoint(sq, im0, e) == e and adjoint(sq, im0, f) == GA.neg(f)
    assert adjoint(sq, im4, en[0]) == en[0] and adjoint(sq, im4, e) != e


def check_number_parity_and_sector_projectors_are_self_adjoint_for_every_adapted_split():
    premise("tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors")
    for m, mats in ((2, M2), (3, M3)):
        sq, n = number(m)
        gamma = ONE
        for k in range(m):
            gamma = prod(sq, gamma, GA.gen(2 * k + 1), GA.gen(2 * k))
        sectors = []
        for j in range(m + 1):
            q = ONE
            for i in range(m + 1):
                if i != j:
                    q = prod(sq, q, lin((F(1, j - i), n), (F(-i, j - i), ONE)))
            sectors.append(q)
        total = {}
        for q in sectors:
            total = GA.add(total, q)
        assert clean(total) == ONE and all(prod(sq, q, q) == q for q in sectors)
        assert [tau(q) * 2 ** m for q in sectors] == ([1, 2, 1] if m == 2 else [1, 3, 3, 1])
        for A, Ainv in mats:
            _, images = reflection(m, A, Ainv)
            assert adjoint(sq, images, n) == n and adjoint(sq, images, gamma) == gamma
            assert all(adjoint(sq, images, q) == q for q in sectors)
            _, en, fn, vn, wn = frame(m, A, Ainv)
            nn = {}
            for k in range(m):
                nn = GA.add(nn, prod(sq, wn[k], vn[k]))
            assert clean(nn) == n


def check_functionals_real_for_all_adapted_splits_are_functions_of_the_number():
    premise("tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors")
    premise("synthesis.premise-positivity-of-values")
    dims = []
    for m, mats in ((1, M1), (2, M2), (3, M3)):
        ker, blades = common_real(m, mats)
        powers = power_functionals(m)
        assert GA.rank_of_vectors(powers) == m + 1 == GA.rank_of_vectors(ker + powers)
        dims.append(len(ker))
    assert dims == [2, 3, 4]
    # one split only, and the diagonal splits only, leave more
    assert len(common_real(1, M1[:1])[0]) == 3 and len(common_real(2, M2[:1])[0]) == 10
    assert len(common_real(2, M2_DIAGONAL)[0]) == 4


def check_pair_state_depends_on_the_split_and_common_states_stay_at_two():
    premise("synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-algebra-and-its-klein-twist-to-the-tensor-product")
    premise("synthesis.chsh-bound-for-two-subsystems-of-a-clifford-algebra-by-a-rational-certificate")
    sq, e, f, v, w = modes(2)
    p = [prod(sq, f[k], e[k]) for k in range(2)]
    gamma = prod(sq, p[0], p[1])
    c, s = F(3, 5), F(4, 5)
    rho = clean(GA.add(prod(sq, lin((F(1, 4), ONE), (F(1, 4), gamma)), lin((1, ONE), (c * c - s * s, p[0]))),
                       GA.scal(c * s, GA.add(prod(sq, w[0], w[1]), prod(sq, v[1], v[0])))))
    assert prod(sq, rho, rho) == rho and tau(rho) == F(1, 4)
    value = lambda x: tau(prod(sq, rho, x)) / tau(rho)
    _, im = reflection(2, *scale(2, 0, 2))
    x = prod(sq, w[0], w[1])
    assert value(x) == F(12, 25) and value(adjoint(sq, im, x)) == F(48, 25)
    # common functionals vanish on u = e_2 f_1 and on odd elements, so only Z Gamma contributes
    ker, blades = common_real(2, M2)
    u = prod(sq, e[1], f[0])
    twist = prod(sq, e[1], p[0])
    for kv in ker:
        om = lambda y: sum(kv[i] * y.get(b, F(0)) for i, b in enumerate(blades))
        assert om(u) == 0 and om(e[0]) == 0 and om(twist) == 0 and om(prod(sq, e[0], p[1])) == 0
        b1 = lin((F(3, 5), twist), (F(4, 5), p[1]))
        b2 = lin((F(4, 5), twist), (F(-3, 5), p[1]))
        chsh = clean(GA.add(prod(sq, e[0], b1), prod(sq, e[0], b2), prod(sq, p[0], b1), GA.neg(prod(sq, p[0], b2))))
        assert om(prod(sq, e[0], twist)) == 0 and om(chsh) == F(7, 5) * om(gamma)
